- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts peak too early and then decline too sharply, indicating an overshoot after spikes, followed by premature mean reversion.
- True outcomes show strong downward momentum after mid-forecast period, suggesting model fails to capture sustained downward pressure.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices in history, failing to adjust forecast downward when true values dip.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true outcomes, which exhibit sharper, more volatile corrections — model lacks sensitivity to short-term volatility.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; true values often dip below forecast before model adjusts.
- Forecasts often overshoot the true mean by 3–5% in early periods, then gradually converge — suggest model has a “warm-up” bias.
- Model fails to account for sharp, sudden drops in late periods (e.g., after 20–25 days), likely due to insufficient horizon-specific calibration.
